correctness.rationale: An exact zero-sum quadratic identity splits all m+n load coordinates into two strictly negative contrast sectors plus the 2x2 global symmetric matrix H(q). Its determinant is a concave quadratic F(q) with exactly one upper root above q=2 and below q=2n/(n-1). This proves all exponents, one-dimensional endpoint kernel and affine embedding rank. Direct root comparison proves strict parameter monotonicity and an implicit-function expansion proves the uniform two-term law. The embedded standalone checker independently reconstructs shortest paths and centered spectra for selected parameter pairs (318 assertions); finite checks are only supplementary. No missing lemmas or infinite extrapolation from numerics are used.

value.rationale: Pineapple graphs are a standard, naturally parameterized family joining a complete graph and a star at one vertex. Ordinary exponent-one gluing is known, whereas the exact breakdown exponent above one, its unique equality direction and Hilbert embedding rank are natural higher-order invariants. The complete two-parameter classification exposes a precise and uniform 1/n effect of adding leaves, with an m-dependent next correction; it provides a quantitative benchmark for stability of negative type under one-point attachment. The star boundary, nonisometric distortion and other graph operations are explicitly excluded. No unsupported broad applications are claimed.
